services.name: School Programs
services.desc: We are pleased to offer school programs, which can be tailored to each class's needs. If you are interested in making a booking, please fill out the below form and staff will respond to your request as soon as possible. The West Vancouver Art Museum’s school programs are uniquely tied to education. In workshops delivered both in the classroom and in the art museum, students will learn about current exhibitions and produce their own art in response. They will also learn about important art movements and historical figures, as well as local Indigenous cultural history through initiatives developed in collaboration with the Squamish Nation. services.name: Rabbit Lane: Douglas Coupland
services.desc: In 1998, Douglas Coupland published Girlfriend in a Coma, a work of fiction that traces the lives of a group of friends from their teenage years through to middle age. Set in West Vancouver, the story centres around Karen McNeil, who falls into a coma that lasts 17 years. When she awakens, the friends come together once again to face an impending apocalypse. The novel, which weaves deftly between literary genres, comes with a moral and a warning.
